source: Ease Up Mush shared glossary. Import this file from any game; the site builds /mush/phraseology/ from it. Do not copy the table into app PLAN/README files.
lede: The games speak Portsmouth. Keep lines short. Don't dump every slang word into every line — sprinkle it so it still reads.

phrases.meaning: Portsmouth. Locals say this; outsiders may still say Portsmouth / *portsmuth*.
A man / bloke. Caring (*“Alright mush.”*), threatening (*“Oi mush.”*), or having a laugh. Default friendly address on the street.
Idiot. Use **rarely**.
Thick / not intelligent. A *dense lad* talks slow, boasts, and misses the point (Steve). Direction for voice, not a word they say about themselves.
Someone who complains about an “injustice” that's trivial to everyone else. You can *be a squinny* or *squinny about* something.
Someone from Southampton.
Calm down. Good after a fight or when someone's winding up.

Lost temper, annoyed, had enough. Can stretch to **copped the needle**. *“He's copped.”* *“She's copped the needle.”* Ongoing: *copping*. *“Alright you don't need to cop about it.”* *“I'm not copping, you're copping.”* Can also mean took a hit of something.
Knock out with a punch (*“I'd bang him out if he said that to me.”*).
Really not fair (*“That's bang out of order.”*). Different from **bang out**.
Knocked out. *“He proper decked him mush.”* Same fight slot as **bang out**; mix them.
Beat up (*“I will batter you.”*). Challenge energy.
Threaten to flatten someone (*“I'll lay 'im out, mush.”*). Same fight slot as **bang out** / **decked**; this one's the threat.
A man. Can shorten to **geez** (*“Oi geez.”*). Same slot as mush; mix them.
Good / crazy. Only people who were young in the **80s** — obscure now; younger voices should not know it.
Something's good. **Rough** speakers only (drunks, denser lads).
OK; also that something is very good.
You don't believe someone. Can stretch to **beard on tash** (*“Beard. Beard on tash.”*).
Steal. *“You going down town on the chore?”* = are you going into town to nick stuff.
Get on the booze. *“I love a shant.”* *“He can ever have a shant.”* *“I got shanted last night.”* *“You were shanted mush.”*
Cheers — let's go and drink. Said once the drinking's been settled on (*“Shant on! Cheers mush.”*). Also does as a shrug when something goes wrong and there's always the pub: *“Oh well. Shant on.”*
Badly hung over.
Happy / proud (*“I'm well chuffed with that.”*). If they're too pleased: *“Alright mush, what do you want, a chuffdy badge?”*
Money (*“Aint got the dosh.”*).
Isn't it. Tag on the end of a line (*“Cushty init.”*).
Down town. How it sounds when spoken (*“I've been dane tane on the shant mush.”*). Pairs with **chore** / **shant**.
Food.
Urinate.
Cigarette (*“Let's have a burn on that then, mush.”*).
Knowledgeable.

notes.title: th → f
notes.body: Drunks and thicker lads replace **th** with **f** in speech — *fink*, *nuffin*, *wiv*, *portsmuth*. Not every street voice: nans, Sir, Choke and Mum stay clearer. Examples: *“I aint never been to portsmuth before.”* *“Who's that mush fink he is?”*

notes.title: Who uses what
notes.body: **Steve** (2nd Avenue) is a dense lad — **cushty**, **init**, **beard**, **fings**. Street lads and trainers lean **mush** / **geezer** plus fight talk (**decked**, **copped**). Kay, the give-way bloke and the bus lad **squinny**; Tom's challenge takes a rare **dinlo**; Gaz and Mick **bang out**; Lee and Kay **bang out of order**; Gaz and Ryan **batter**; Dave, Mick and Ryan take losses with **ease up mush**; Dave and Mick **shant** and **cushty**, and Dave takes a win or a hiding with **shant on**; older nans and 80s voices get a rare **lakes**; denser lads get **beard**, **chore**, **dane tane**, **init** and **chuffed**.
